correctness.rationale: The diagonal is forced to one in characteristic two. The multiplication law reduces u²=1 exactly to AB=0; C is arbitrary. Count rank-r A via Gaussian subspaces and surjections, B columns in ker A and arbitrary C. Normalize with D_s; a uniformly bounded product factor converges to 1/D_infty; discrete Gaussian tails yield the sharp theta prefactors and fixed-q total variation O(q^{-n/2}). Given A of rank r, conditional surjectivity of B has failure O(q^{-r}); averaging under the proved centered law gives O(q^{-n/2}) homological failure. Direct GF2 and GF4 tests in verify.py agree with the formula.

originality.rationale: The direct prior incidence-algebra involution enumeration explicitly excludes characteristic two. Catanzaro–Zabka supply finite-field matrix-rank counts but sample sequentially conditioned maps, not uniformly over the entire AB=0 variety; their limit changes q, not fixed-q growing equal dimensions. The ungraded and real-field random complex results do not imply the sharp fixed-q two-parity law. Remaining uninspected broad variety treatments are a priority risk.
residual_risks: The original 1981 paper of De Concini and Strickland on varieties of complexes was not inspected in full and could contain a more general explicit count from which the exact formula follows.
Unindexed ring-incidence studies or unpublished manuscripts might already discuss characteristic-two square-one counts and their asymptotics.
The exact rank-matrix factor is standard prior work; originality is limited to the structural incidence specialization and sharp parity-law synthesis.

value.rationale: Square-one units of incidence algebras form a natural finite-group invariant. The characteristic-two case is explicitly excluded by relevant prior involution enumerations. The exact spectra for all equal three-level posets, a sharp periodic fixed-field discrete-Gaussian law, and high-probability middle exactness provide a substantive result distinct from the previously studied sequential finite-field random-complex measure.
